ELPQUICK is a prospective cohort study concerning acute abdominal surgery, and it should not be confused with other studies that have similar names [^src1]. Within the broader national quality development efforts of the Danish Regions' Clinical Quality Development Program, the study contributes to the evaluation of clinical indicators for patients presenting with acute abdominal pain, utilizing empirical data from 2022–2023 [^src1]. 

The primary significance of the ELPQUICK study lies in its scientific validation of early medical interventions. Alongside the AHA study, ELPQUICK provides evidence that early antibiotic treatment reduces mortality in acute abdominal surgery [^src1]. This finding directly legitimizes the focus of [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], which monitors early antibiotic administration as a critical quality metric [^src1]. By demonstrating that early antibiotic treatment is one of the specific measures that has successfully lowered mortality rates in this surgical field, ELPQUICK serves as a foundational piece of evidence for operational recommendations and standard adjustments aimed at improving diagnostic certainty and patient survival in acute care settings [^src1].
